method_changes: Unsigned and bool vector unary minus through explicit scalar VectorNegationComponent policy; narrow signed and floating behavior retained.
Boolean value, assignment, scalar multiplication/division, Dot, cwiseAbs, SquareModulus, Modulus, Cross, Normalize/Normalized and GetLERP use native promoted truth tables.
Default Vec2/3/4 and Vec4 planar constructor use explicit i32 ElementCast(0), independently of custom Default.
DX/DY/DZ use native integer constructor constants, supporting i8, bool and custom ElementCast elements.
Mat4 adjoint retains its existing MatrixScalar+Neg bounds and VectorArithmeticComponent::vector_negate dispatch through a focused helper.

original_assertion_audit.result: Read all five original declarations and Rust translations: same input values, cube point ordering, component writes, matrix translation, and 0.001 tolerance. Component equality checks are consolidated into tuple assertions; both matrix norm assertions retained.

remaining_gaps: Custom unary-negation elements must implement VectorNegationComponent explicitly; arbitrary C++ unary expression template deduction is represented by this Rust policy.
Native integer-constant construction requires i32: ElementCast<T>; custom Rust Default/From<u8> alone no longer supplies native zero/unit behavior.
Custom C++ constructors, copy/move/destructor hooks, overload side effects, floating environment flags and undefined behavior domains are not exhaustively modeled.
Division by false is undefined natively; Rust reports the offending false divisor with a panic, an explicitly excluded native domain.
i128/u128 policies remain Rust extensions; no OCCT standard-primitive parity claim for those widths.
Protected ABI/layout, all platform/compiler configurations and full template-instantiation closure remain unproven.
